title: Row symmetry transfer
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, and $q$ a rational number. Suppose $\sigma$ is a register state and $dd$ is a natural number such that $\sigma.n-\sigma.u=dd$, each register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, and $\sigma.u\le\sigma.n$. If every encoded edge from a row $u'$ with $\sigma.u\le u'<\sigma.n$ to a column $w'<\sigma.n$ is present exactly when the reverse edge is present, then for all $p,a,b,w\le B$, the probabilistic semantics of the program from state $s0$, with $u$ set to $\sigma.n$ and $w,p,a,b$ set to those values, has acceptance probability $q$. If this row-symmetry condition fails and $q=0$, then the program from state $y0$ and register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.

replaced:
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $dd$ a
natural number. Suppose $\sigma.n-\sigma.u=dd$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most
$B$, $2\sigma.n+2+2\sigma.n^2\le B$, and $\sigma.u\le\sigma.n$. If the encoded adjacency
relation is symmetric for every row $u'$ from $\sigma.u$ up to but not including
$\sigma.n$ and every column $w'<\sigma.n$, then for all $p,a,b,w\le B$, the program at
state $s0$ with $u$ reset to $\sigma.n$ and $w,p,a,b$ set to those values has
probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If that row-symmetry condition
fails, then $q=0$ implies the program at state $y0$ with record $\sigma$ has
probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
